headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/data-flow confusion from Copilot’s editor/repo context, but Whisper is read-only and offline so most pairwise harms stay low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot ingests editor buffers and repo context by default, so malicious text in files could influence its outputs. Whisper only processes audio files and has no interactive instruction channel, so there is no direct bridge from Whisper back into Copilot. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited and mostly manual or file-mediated.
conditions: IF Copilot is pointed at attacker-controlled repository text that later gets copied into prompts or files
IF Whisper transcripts are manually pasted into Copilot as instructions
mitigations: Review Copilot-generated edits before applying
Keep untrusted text out of repo files used as prompt context
Use separate folders for audio/transcript artifacts and code
Disable copy-paste of raw transcripts into coding prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to generated transcripts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot can read open editor buffers and repo context, while Whisper reads audio files; neither profile shows shared filesystem access or outbound third-party upload from Whisper. Copilot’s network egress is vendor-only, but the pair does not expose a documented shared workspace or secret-handling path, so leakage risk is limited to operator-mediated file placement.
conditions: IF sensitive audio transcripts are stored in the same repo context Copilot reads
IF the operator places confidential text into files that Copilot can access
mitigations: Store transcripts outside code repositories
Use separate access-controlled directories for audio and code
Avoid placing secrets in open editor buffers
Delete temporary transcript files after use
requires-engineering: enforce workspace segregation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Whisper cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is Copilot’s mutable repo access versus Whisper’s read-only audio-file processing. No locking issue is documented for Whisper, so conflict remains small.
conditions: IF Copilot and another editor instance target the same git worktree simultaneously
IF Whisper-derived artifacts are manually committed while Copilot is editing the same files
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits in the same worktree
Commit or stash before running Copilot Workspace edits
Keep Whisper outputs in separate directories
Use one editor session per branch
requires-engineering: add file-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can generate code or edits from repo context, and Whisper can produce transcripts from audio, but neither profile shows built-in verification of the other’s outputs. If Whisper transcripts are copied into Copilot prompts or Copilot edits are accepted without review, errors can cascade into downstream code changes. The pathway exists in default human workflows.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are used as authoritative input to Copilot without human verification
IF Copilot Workspace edits are applied without review
mitigations: Verify transcripts against the original audio
Review Copilot diffs before applying
Mark transcript confidence in filenames or comments
Use a second reviewer for generated code
requires-engineering: add automated transcript-to-audio checks

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context and vendor-only egress, while Whisper is open-source and local by profile. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for the pair, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling of code and audio artifacts rather than a specific breach class.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Copilot-accessible repo context
IF audio files contain regulated content and are stored under policies incompatible with local processing
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Copilot context
Use local-only storage for audio artifacts
Apply retention rules to transcript files
Document data-class handling for both tools
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency review
